title: The Blue Dress
subtitle: The question I wasn't supposed to ask
label: New essay
alt_text: Public domain painting The Sisters by Wilfrid de Glehn (two women in pale blue dresses) full-bleed, fading to dark, with the title The Blue Dress and subtitle The question I wasn't supposed to ask. Not Plain.

slides.text: I always asked my mom why I wasn’t allowed to go to North Carolina with my sister every year when her summer trip was planned.

slides.label: Sar
slides.text: That’s not my name. It’s incomplete, suffocated by her breath…

slides.label: 11 years old
slides.text: But here I am, 11 years old, chubby, but not that chubby, feeling as inadequate as I always do, and suddenly a new question pops into my head.
My ears fill with the pressure of my blood.

captions.facebook:
“I always asked my mom why I wasn’t allowed to go to North Carolina with my sister every year when her summer trip was planned.”

I’m 11, crowded into a JCPenney dressing room with my mom and my sister, who is trying on a pretty blue dress. I ask about the trip again. And then a new question pops into my head, one I had never thought to ask.

pinterest.description: At 11, crowded into a JCPenney dressing room with her mom and sister, the author asks again why she is never allowed to join her sister's summer trip to North Carolina, and then a new question she had never thought to ask. A true story about sisters and family, from a narrative nonfiction memoir in progress. From Not Plain, a memoir newsletter by Sarah.
